source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
1. Enter BMC-Web -> Click tab "Settings" -> Click "User Management" to view user accounts.    
2. Change a exists user's password.
3. Change a exists user's name.
4. Change a exists user's privilege.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. You can change password successfully and you only can use new password to login.
2. You can change name successfully and you only can use new name to login.
3. You can change privilege successfully and you can only use the function that the privilege can use.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: curl + jq (Web UI action by operator)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Modify user account - WebUI is driven through the BMC Web UI by the operator (add/delete/modify a user + set privileges). Agent verifies the resulting account list: curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts 2>&1 | jq ".Members[]?|{Id,UserName,RoleId}" 2>/dev/null after the operator acts.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL Redfish account-list JSON after the WebUI modify user account so the user confirms the account was added/deleted/modified as expected.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: account add/delete/modify is a security-sensitive write done in the Web UI by the operator; agent only reads the resulting list.

historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires one disposable account, immutable ID, one property per approved action, complete state/audit after each, old/new credential and session behavior, non-destructive role enforcement, independent recovery and cleanup.

original_test_intent: Verify the BMC WebUI independently changes a disposable account's password, username and privilege, with only new credentials/identity accepted and effective permissions restricted to the new role, while recovery and unrelated accounts remain intact.
original_method: Identify a disposable account by immutable ID; preserve complete account/role/session/audit baseline and recovery; define old/new protected password, supported username rename and least-privilege role matrix; after separate approvals change one property at a time in source order; capture UI/audit and full readback; prove old/new authentication, session invalidation, identity resolution and allowed/denied actions; restore or delete only the disposable account.
manual_activity: An owner approves the disposable account, old/new values, username support, role matrix, session behavior and recovery/cleanup. A human operates and visually checks each source WebUI change separately. Automation may collect complete redacted state/audit and bounded auth/authorization evidence but cannot expose secrets, combine steps or issue the verdict.
required_inputs: Immutable disposable account ID and protected-account exclusions
Password policy, protected old/new password and session rules
Supported old/new username and identity/duplicate semantics
Current/target role and allowed/denied action matrix
safety_requirements: Never modify protected/default/recovery/production accounts or expose old/new passwords, tokens or sessions in screenshots, commands, logs or JSON.
Verify immutable target, complete baseline, separate recovery and approved final state before the first change; do not clear security logs.
Change password, then username if supported, then privilege one at a time with separate point-of-action approval and readback; do not batch or retry.
After password change, prove old secret denial, new-secret login and defined session invalidation without disrupting recovery.
After rename, prove immutable ID continuity, old-name denial/new-name login and no duplicate/partial identity; after role change, test approved allowed and denied non-destructive actions.
Stop on wrong identity, secret exposure, unexpected privilege, continued old access, recovery impact or cleanup mismatch; restore via independent recovery without editing another account.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target/account, policies, three transition matrices, baseline, recovery and cleanup; present each WebUI change separately for approval.
After each approved change, capture redacted UI/audit and complete account/session readback tied to immutable ID.
Run bounded old/new authentication, session and non-destructive authorization checks appropriate to that property while confirming local-admin continuity.
Restore/delete only the disposable account as approved, reconcile baseline, archive evidence and stop without retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve disposable identity, old/new password/name/role values, session behavior and allowed/denied matrix.
Approve each WebUI change, independent recovery and exact restore/delete cleanup.
Review per-property state/auth/session/authorization/audit evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its API list can corroborate username/role but `-k`, inline credentials, partial fields and no sessions are unsafe/incomplete. It cannot prove password change, old/new login, session invalidation, effective permissions or source WebUI behavior.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the exact source WebUI controls for one property at a time with protected secret entry, complete trusted account/session/audit readback and bounded auth/role checks; do not substitute generic API edits.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The password, username and privilege changes, their three Criteria, WebUI path, no Script, DeepSeek proposal/risk and 5/0-minute estimates remain preserved independently.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute three separately approved WebUI transitions on one immutable disposable account, verifying state, old/new authentication/session behavior and actual least-privilege authorization after each, then restore.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC WebUI User Management account editor and account/session services.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, WebUI build, account/session schema and browser/client versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor account/password/rename/role/session specification and Project access-control/recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds disposable scope, immutable identity, protected secrets, per-step state/auth/authorization evidence and recovery while retaining all source changes.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: API state does not prove WebUI control; role readback does not prove effective privilege; final state does not prove the three intermediate transitions.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Disposable ID, policies, old/new values, role matrix, baseline, recovery and cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Password/name changes can lock out the test identity; role change can escalate access; existing sessions may retain rights until invalidation.

project_override_considerations: Browser automation or vendor API may be approved only when the original WebUI path, actual method, reason, engineer approval, per-property auth/session/role equivalence and uncovered UI coverage are recorded. Read-only list output is not equivalent.
expected_evidence: Approved BMC/account immutable ID, protected exclusions, three transition matrices, complete redacted account/role/session baseline and recovery proof
Per-property WebUI screenshots/DOM and audit with secrets redacted plus complete immutable-ID state readback
Password old-secret denial/new-secret login and expected session invalidation
Username old-name denial/new-name login with immutable-ID continuity; role allowed/denied action evidence
Exact cleanup/final baseline, unrelated/local-admin continuity, preserved logs/no retry and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require password, username and privilege modification with corresponding functional outcomes. Platform policies and exact values are readiness inputs, not conflicting purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The three modification objectives are explicit. A disposable account, supported policies, role matrix and recovery can be supplied, so execution is pending rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but separates all three source changes, replaces insecure list-only evidence with old/new auth/session/role behavior and adds protected scope and cleanup.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its critical controls and sharpens immutable-ID continuity and independent checkpointing after every property.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic post-list confirmation with three auditable security state transitions.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps Add/Delete separate; neither proves password/name/privilege modification behavior.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents modification of a protected account, password leakage or privilege escalation and prevents a final account list from being mistaken for three successful behavioral transitions.
independent_technical_reasoning: Password, username and role modify different security properties and have distinct proof: credential validity/session invalidation, identity continuity/name lookup and effective authorization. Combining them destroys fault isolation and can strand the test account. Each transition must be approved, observed and verified separately against the same immutable disposable identity with independent recovery.
